summary: This code creates a fun easter egg that detects when a user switches away from the browser tab and changes the page title and favicon to show a 'sleeping meerkat' message. When they come back to the tab, it restores the original title and favicon. The effect sets up a listener for visibility changes and cleans it up when the component unmounts.

explanations.3: useBaseUrl() is a helper function that converts a relative image path into a full URL based on your site's configuration, so the favicon image can be found no matter where the site is deployed.
explanations.9: document.querySelector() finds the first HTML element matching the selector — in this case, the <link> tag that points to the site's icon in the browser tab.
explanations.10: The ?. (optional chaining) operator safely accesses the href property only if faviconLink exists; if it's null, it just returns undefined instead of crashing.
explanations.13: document.hidden is a built-in property that's true when the current tab is not visible to the user (they've switched to another tab or window).
explanations.22: addEventListener() registers the handleVisibilityChange function to run whenever the browser fires a 'visibilitychange' event (when the tab becomes hidden or visible).
explanations.23: This return statement defines a cleanup function that runs when the component unmounts; it removes the event listener to prevent memory leaks.
explanations.25: The dependency array includes location and sleepingFaviconUrl so the effect re-runs if either of these values change, ensuring the listener stays in sync with any page navigation or favicon URL updates.
